root_cause.text: The context entry teardown in the Intel VT-d driver cleared the entire 128-bit context entry (via multiple 64-bit writes) without first clearing the Present bit, allowing the IOMMU hardware to observe an inconsistent “torn” entry where the Present bit was still set while other fields were zeroed, leading to unpredictable behavior or spurious faults.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: “the current implementation zeros the entire 128-bit entry using multiple 64-bit writes. This creates a window where the hardware can fetch a 'torn' entry — where some fields are already zeroed while the 'Present' bit is still set — leading to unpredictable behavior or spurious faults.” The patch adds a separate `context_clear_present()` call (clearing only the Present bit) before the invalidation step, and defers the full zeroing (`context_clear_entry()`) until after invalidation is complete, implementing the proper ownership handshake per VT-d spec Section 6.5.3.3.
